High-growth in the South West
Mapping out the most ambitious 
businesses in the South West of England

We use 8 criteria to identify 
high-growth and ambitious 
companies. Each of these are a sign 
of external validation that a business 
is either actively growing or creating 
ambitious growth plans. 
All companies featured in this report 
have met at least one of these 
growth triggers.
What do we mean by “ambitious”?
Equity investment
Accelerator attendance
Scaleups
MBO/MBI
Venture debt
Grant recipients
High-growth lists
Academic spinouts

There are 1613 active, ambitious 
companies in the South West, 7% 
of the UK’s total.
Since 2011, an additional 120 have 
exited the market, either through 
an IPO or an acquisition, and 243 
are no longer trading.  
The distribution of stages of 
evolution in the region is roughly in 
keeping with the national average.

51% of high-growth companies in the 
South West have used equity funding 
to grow since 2011. This figure varies 
across the region, with 43% of 
companies in Wiltshire using equity 
to grow, compared to 56% in 
Cornwall.
19% have received grants and 17% 
have achieved scaleup status.

2019 has already been a stellar year of 
funding for the South West. The first 
quarter has been the highest on 
record, thanks in large part to an 
injection of £200m into Bristol based 
OVO Energy from Mitsubishi 
Corporation. 
This means that 10% of the UK’s 
announced equity funding in 2019 so 
far has gone to companies in the 
South West. 
 
Fundraising statistics
NUMBER OF DEALS AND AMOUNT RAISED

The biggest destination for funding is, 
unsurprisingly, around Bristol and Bath. 
These cities are home to a number of 
well funded companies alongside OVO 
Energy, including semiconductor 
company Xmos (£43.6m), its AI spinout 
Graphcore (£244m),  and pioneering AR 
company Ultrahaptics (£74.4m).
This cluster of companies helps make 
Bristol a leading tech centre in the UK.
Geographical distribution
NUMBER OF DEALS COMPLETED BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES

There’s also a large investment hub in 
Cornwall, where the biggest fundraising 
recipient is Goonhilly Earth Station, 
having raised a total of £24.7m. 
GES is part of the Aerohub Enterprise 
Zone, just one of the developments that 
upholds the region’s reputation as a centre 
for Aerospace technology. 30 high-growth 
aerospace companies in the UK (15%) are 
headquartered in the South West.

24% of high-growth companies in the South 
West have a female founder, the second 
highest rate in England after the North East. 
So far in 2019, 20% of deals in the South West 
have gone to female founders - the highest on 
record - but they received just 4% of pounds 
invested. This figure increases to 13% if we 
discount OVO Energy’s megadeal. 
2013 was the only year in which the average 
amount raised was higher for female founders 
than their male counterparts - £1.35m 
compared to £1.25m.

The top investors are a mix of 
government backed money, EIS fund 
managers and patient capital. 
BGF tops the list with 10 deals since 
the start of 2018, the largest of which 
was an £11.5m investment into 
Cornwall based clothing brand 
Seasalt.
